## Monte Carlo probability revalidation

- version: `2.0.0` · cells 30 · games per cell 256
- all gates pass: **false**
- failing: `sideBiasPerCellWithinTolerance`
- max absolute per-cell side bias: **0.0781** against a frozen threshold of 0.05
- mean across cells -0.0064 ± 0.0049, t -1.2901, systematic **false**
- per-cell standard error at this sample size: 0.0313

Phase 6C2C1 recorded this same gate as FAIL, with a max per-cell side bias of 0.0625 against the same frozen threshold of 0.05. See docs/simulation-v3/phase-6c2c1-limitations.md.

This phase changed no parameter values, so it cannot have moved this metric through calibration. The per-cell figures did shift because Phase 6C2C2 randomised the opening possession, which changes every game's seeded sequence.

**On the gate's power.** The frozen threshold of 0.05 sits at 1.60 per-cell standard errors (SE 0.0313), and the observed maximum of 0.0781 sits at 2.49. The expected maximum of 30 independent standard normal draws is about 2.4, so a per-cell MAXIMUM compared against a fixed absolute threshold with no multiplicity correction will exceed it in most runs by construction. This is offered as analysis of the gate's power, NOT as a re-scored pass: the gate is frozen, it FAILS, and it is recorded as failing.

Frozen threshold unchanged: **true**.

The dedicated side-symmetry suite, which does apply Benjamini-Hochberg control across its 48 cells, passes all 10 of its gates over 240,000 paired games with an aggregate advantage of -0.11pp and 0 cells beyond +/-2pp.
